title: autoscaler-affinity-inference-gradual-degradation-and-reserve-inefficiency
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We received multiple customer escalations (two enterprise customers: HelixPay and NovaRetail) reporting intermittent capacity shortfalls across their reserved pools over a 48-hour window. Symptoms looked like: requests queued for minutes, burst budget drained unexpectedly, and the autoscaler not replenishing headroom despite sustained traffic. This ticket tracks the investigation, immediate mitigations, root cause, and proposed permanent fixes.

Key observations:
- The degradation was gradual over ~6 hours per incident, not an instant pool depletion event.
- Telemetry shows autoscaler issued repeated scale-downs for affected pools while tenant-level request latency increased — indicating a miscorrelation between observed per-slot utilization and expected headroom need.
- Affected tenants had mixed traffic patterns (short synchronous requests + infrequent long-running streams) and relied on KV cache affinity to improve latency.
- Our fallback/burst accounting logs show reserved burst credits were billed but not made available to active slots due to an allocator mismatch (slots flagged as cold/unallocated while KV caches remained warm).

Hypothesis (root cause summary):
1) Affinity inference service (affinity-agent) was using a decayed-window estimator to classify slot hotness. A regression (introduced in affinity-agent v1.7.2) applied an overly aggressive decay when estimating cross-tenant sticky usage, causing hot slots to be marked as cold sooner than they actually were.
2) The autoscaler uses the affinity signal combined with a headroom projection to decide scale-downs. Because affinity inference undercounted warm slots, the autoscaler believed there was excess capacity and performed scale-downs. Scale-downs in turn forced in-flight requests to fallback into burst allocations, depleting burst credit unexpectedly.
3) Separately, the allocator's slot-claim path had a race where slots transitioning from warm->cold were not cleared from the reserved-ledger promptly, producing an artificial underreporting of available burst-capable slots to the burst-manager.

Immediate mitigations applied (timeline):
- 2026-03-10 04:12 UTC: Customer escalation from HelixPay support; oncall triaged. (Pager duty: Liam O'Connor)
- 2026-03-10 05:00 UTC: Emergency guardrail: increased autoscaler min_headroom for all reserved pools by +15% via feature-flag (FF:autoscaler_min_headroom_override). Link: https://console.redwood.ai/flags/FF-autoscaler-min-headroom
- 2026-03-10 05:20 UTC: Temporary burst-provisioning override applied for impacted tenants enabling direct reserved-slot pinning (internal runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Reserved+Pin+Runbook).
- 2026-03-11 02:10 UTC: Rolled back affinity-agent v1.7.2 to v1.7.1 in the affected region(s) (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/affinity-agent/pull/483).
- 2026-03-11 03:45 UTC: Hotfix merged to allocator to clear stale reserved-ledger entries on state transition (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/2301). Deployed as canary to 5% traffic, observed smoothing of burst-accounting.

Investigation details and evidence:
- Dashboards: reserved-pool-utilization (dash: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/6/reserved-pool-utilization) shows stepwise drop in 'per-slot active_mark' metric preceding scale-down events by ~9-12 minutes.
- Logs: affinity-agent logs show anomalous decay coefficients (alpha) at the time of incidents: alpha toggled from 0.92 -> 0.3 due to a misapplied config merge during release.
- Traces: end-to-end sampling captured a tenant request sequence where KV cache hits persisted but the slot was reclaimed and returned to scheduler within 4 minutes.

Proposed permanent fixes (epics/tasks):
- Fix 1: affinity-agent: correct decay logic and add configurable safe floor for decay coefficient; add unit + integration tests validating hotness signals across synthetic workloads. (ENG-582402 planned follow-up).
- Fix 2: autoscaler: add a delay-buffer when acting on affinity-derived scale signals (safety window of 12 minutes default) and surface an alert if autoscaler performs >N scale-downs for a specific pool within M minutes.
- Fix 3: allocator: ensure reserved-ledger entry removal is idempotent and atomic with slot state transitions. Add property-based tests to catch race conditions.
- Fix 4: burst-manager audit: add a reconciliation job that cross-checks burst credits vs slot-assignment every 1 minute and raises a high-severity alert on mismatch >5%.

Acceptance criteria for completion:
- affinity-agent deploys v1.7.3 with regression fix and passes new e2e tests in canary cluster (canary run 48 hours with no incidents).
- autoscaler changed to include safety window and we observe no customer-facing scale-down-induced bursts in 14-day canary.
- allocator hotfix fully rolled out and reconciliation job shows <0.5% mismatch over 7 days.
- Postmortem drafted and published to Confluence, customer-facing communication drafted and reviewed by PM/Comms.

Customer communication plan:
- Short-term: Customers were notified on 2026-03-10 with temporary mitigations applied. (HelixPay case: INC-2026-3301, NovaRetail: INC-2026-3304).
- Long-term: Prepare a technical follow-up noting root cause, timeline, fixes, and mitigations performed. Draft review with PM Sarah Patel and Legal for wording.

Next steps / Ownership:
- Liam O'Connor: lead hotfix rollout and monitoring (assignee).
- Maya Chen: own affinity-agent regression fix and tests (creator).
- Rajiv Menon: allocator reconciliation job + property tests.
- Sarah Patel (PM): craft customer communications and track SLAs.

Links and artifacts:
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Reserved+Pin+Runbook
- Affinity PR (rollback): https://github.com/redwood-inference/affinity-agent/pull/483
- Allocator PR (stale-ledger fix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/2301
- ONCALL notes: internal slack thread https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/GBURST1234/p167852
- Dashboards: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/6/reserved-pool-utilization

Risks and trade-offs considered:
- Increasing min_headroom reduces efficiency/cost for customers but buys stability; customers were notified and agreed to temporary cost impact for availability.
- Adding autoscaler safety window increases latency of scale-downs and may hold unneeded capacity longer — mitigated by dynamic windowing based on pool volatility heuristics.
- Reconciliation job adds additional load to control plane (lightweight queries every minute); evaluated at scale and considered acceptable with sharding.

Postmortem plan and timeline:
- Draft postmortem by 2026-03-17 (owner: Liam O'Connor).
- Review with Eng leadership and PM by 2026-03-18.
- Customer-ready summary and change log published by 2026-03-21.
